newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan PGM traders wary despite Russia assurances.
newsitem.headline: Japan PGM traders wary despite Russia assurances.

text.p: Japanese platinum group metal (PGM) traders on Wednesday said Russia's assurance there would be no delays in PGM exports did little to relieve the market, which would remain nervous until supplies were to emerge.

The traders said they were concerned that PGM prices, especially those of palladium, may not fall as much as they would like to see even after Russia resumes exports, leading to a decline in Japan's appetite for the metals in the long term.
"We will not be relieved until (Russian) metal supplies start flowing into the market. The demand/supply situation in Japan is extremely tight," one trading house trader said.
"Inventories at some Japanese auto makers and some electronic makers are at critically low levels," he said.

Sergei Gorny, deputy director of Russia's PGMs export agent Almazjuvelirexport (Almaz), said there would be no further delays, but that Russian 1997 platinum and palladium exports would be down from last year.
He also said Russia would not sell more PGMs than necessary this year.
The six-month suspension of Russian exports, caused by bureaucratic problems there, sent world palladium and platinum prices soaring and caused an acute supply tightness.
Russia is the world's top supplier of palladium, providing more than 60 percent of supplies, and Japan is the world's largest consumer of PGM.

Some end-users, such as makers of computer chips and auto catalysts, loathing the high prices and expecting Russian spot sales to resume soon, have refrained from buying supplies this month, aggravating the domestic tightness in supplies.
"Unless Russia sells a larger volume of PGMs in the spot market than it has agreed to sell under term contracts, prices will not fall significantly," a precious metal industry source said.
"Doubts over Russia's reliability as a stable metal supplier will never disappear, which would inevitably dampen Japan's palladium demand," he said.
The precious metal industry source said: "Several traders are planning to buy Russian palladium in the spot market before they receive term contract deliveries by mid-July."
However no signs of Russia's return to the spot market have emerged yet and traders have been forced to scramble for supplies in the very tight market, he said.
Japanese clients have signed PGM contracts with Russia for deliveries from July to December. The first supplies are due to arrive in Japan at around July 10-15.
Officials of U.S.-based hedge fund, Tiger Management, which is believed to hold 1.5 million ounces of palladium, visited Japan in June to seek potential long-term customers.
No Japanese companies are believed to have signed contracts with the fund, traders said.
